chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad narrated from Ubaydullah ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Qalanisi, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abul Jarood, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'You will keep extending your eyes toward a man, saying:

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far, referring to Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (as)
key_terms.تَمُدُّونَ أَعْيُنَكُمْ: You extend your eyes (metaphor for fixing attention/hoping)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'extending eyes' in the context of waiting for the Mahdi?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (as) addresses the historical phenomenon of 'Gharb al-Mahdi' (the death of claimed Mahdis) by attributing it to divine concealment, where the true Imam remains unknown until the appointed time. It underscores the Shia concept of 'al-Intizar al-Faraj' (waiting for relief) as a period of active anticipation rather than passive speculation, emphasizing that the true identity is known only to Allah. This narrative reinforces the theological principle that the Imam's existence is hidden from public scrutiny until God wills his emergence.
